Ronaldo is officially retired from the Portugal international team 💔 | A random Thursday 💔 | DM for edit ideas |  Cristiano Ronaldo officially announced his retirement from international football on Thursday, November 5, 2026, bringing a close to an extraordinary 23-year career with the Portugal national team. The 41-year-old legend shared the news via an emotional social media video, stating that the time had come to "hand back the number 7 shirt" and pass it on to the next generation. While he is stepping away from the national team, Ronaldo is not retiring from professional soccer entirely; he will continue playing at the club level for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia as he pursues his milestone 1,000th career goal. Reasons Behind the Decision Ronaldo's sudden retirement follows weeks of escalating tension and a public fallout with Portugal's head coach, Jorge Jesus. The dispute peaked during the October international window when Ronaldo was left on the bench as an unused substitute during a Nations League match against Norway. Accusing Jesus of breaking promises regarding his playing time, Ronaldo abruptly walked out of the national team's training camp, resulting in a fine and a 30-day suspension from the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF). A Record-Breaking Legacy Ronaldo retires as the most accomplished men's international footballer of all time, holding the world records for both appearances and goals: • Caps: 234 appearances • Goals: 146 goals • Major Trophies: UEFA Euro 2016, plus two UEFA Nations League titles (2019, 2025) • World Cup Milestone: Earlier in 2026, he became the first player in football history to play and score in six consecutive FIFA World Cups.
